messages.subject: Have Vim-R-plugin source shell configuration?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Does anyone know of a way to have vim-r source my .zshrc when spawning a console?

I currently have a custom R_LIBS directory specified there which does not get included, resulting in the vim-r console not being able to find many libraries.

A simple work-around would be to hard-code the path into my .Rprofile, but since the path varies from system to system, I would rather have the shell deal with it.

Any ideas?
Keith

messages.subject: Re: Have Vim-R-plugin source shell configuration?
messages.body_plain:
I think this is a Tmux configuration issue, and, perhaps this helps: http://superuser.com/questions/253786/how-can-i-make-tmux-use-my-default-shell

If R is running in an external terminal (if either you are using GVim or Vim isn't already inside Tmux), in addition to editing your ~/.tmux.conf, you will also need to put in your vimrc:

let vimrplugin_notmuxconf = 1

messages.subject: compile pdf without R
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am wondering if there is a possibility to compile a pdf document without evaluating R chunks enclosed with <<>>= @
Why I need it, it is because now I am writing a text, and from time to time I want to produce a pdf that other people can read, but I do not want to rerun everything including the R code.
R chunks were previously evaluated, some of them cached some not.

Or maybe there is a better routine?

Thanks,
Olga

messages.subject: Re: Omni completion
messages.body_plain:
The "VimCom port" is opened by the R package vimcom.plus. When the vimcom.plus library is loaded, it checks if the environment variable VIMRPLUGIN_TMPDIR is set. If R was started by Vim, the variable will be set and, then, the vimcom.plus package starts a server listening on port 9999. So, you have to load the vimcom.plus every time that you start R. However, instead of doing this manually, you can put in your .Rprofile:

library(vimcom.plus)

The command :RpluginConfig puts the above line in the user's Rprofile. Thus the command :RpluginConfig should be run only once.

messages.body_plain:
On Wednesday, January 22, 2014 9:26:20 PM UTC-3, yarosla...@gmail.com wrote:
> update: some variables from GlobalEnv list populate on C-X C-O, while some do not.

All R workspace variables should be available for omnicompletion. Of course, if you press ^X^O after some characters, these characters will be treated as the beginning of the object name to complete and only objects that have the same characters at the beginning of their names will populate the pop up menu.
